scope: One-sided capacity floor for the intensively surveyed South African Mapungubwe landscape, not the wider 30,000 km2 polity

promotion_audit.decision: The 2021 archaeological reconstruction is an aggregate of the capital and 114 ordinary homesteads in the South African survey landscape. It reports 10,700 contemporaneous people for the AD 1270-1320 Mapungubwe phase. The surveyed National Park plus buffer footprint is wholly contained by the EU5 mapungubwe location, and archaeobotanical, archaeozoological and land-use evidence identifies local grain, pulses, livestock, game and river fish. The record is therefore used only to require the containing EU5 geography to support at least 10,700 people; it is not a two-sided scale anchor.

records.label: Mapungubwe National Park and buffer-zone settlement survey, AD 1270-1320
records.interval_semantics: Huffman and Woodborne (2021), Table 2 and pp. 3-4, reconstruct 5,700 people in 114 ordinary homesteads plus 5,000 at the capital, totalling 10,700 people in the South African portion of the Shashe-Limpopo valley during the AD 1270-1320 Mapungubwe phase. The authors stress that the method is relative rather than an absolute census, so 10,700 is retained only as a one-sided observed-support floor. The local-food interval is deliberately broad: staple crops, pulses, livestock, game and fish are evidenced locally, while long-distance trade is evidenced for prestige/export goods rather than staple food; no precise calorie share is published.
pressure_evidence: Huffman and Woodborne (2021), pp. 2-4 and Table 2: systematic foot surveys in Mapungubwe National Park and its buffer recorded about 1,150 Iron Age sites; 114 contemporaneous ordinary homesteads plus the capital yield a reconstructed Mapungubwe-phase total of 10,700 people.

Huffman and Woodborne (2021), pp. 2-3: intensive agriculture was a critical agent of change; the surveyed land-use system cultivated sorghum on rich wet vlei margins and millet on sandy fluvial terraces, with grainbins, cattle kraals, cattle posts and field camps distributed through the landscape.

SANParks, Natural and Cultural History, Middle Iron Age sections: excavated settlements preserve sorghum, millet, beans and cowpeas and bones of cattle, sheep and goats, supplemented by local game and river fish; farmers cleared fields and used seasonally flooded Limpopo land.

Huffman and Woodborne (2021), pp. 4-5 and Table 3: repeated severe droughts affected agricultural production, ritual grainbin burning and political stability; the AD 1310 +/- 5 drought contributed to abandonment by about AD 1320. This is independent resource-pressure evidence, but the climatic shock prevents a two-sided saturation interpretation.

UNESCO dossier 1099bis: the protected 28,168.6602-ha property contains the capital sites and the settlement area dependent on them and is enclosed by a 104,800-ha buffer, providing a bounded South African comparison footprint rather than the wider transfrontier kingdom.
records.trade_dependence: Long-distance Indian Ocean trade supplied wealth and prestige goods and exported gold and ivory. No cited source demonstrates imported staple calories; local crops, pulses, livestock, game and river fish are directly evidenced. The 0.80-1.00 local-food interval preserves uncertainty and the observation is used only as a lower bound.
records.boundary_description: The South African Origins of Mapungubwe survey footprint: Mapungubwe National Park / UNESCO property (281.686602 km2) and its surrounding 1,048 km2 buffer zone at the Limpopo-Shashe confluence. This is the bounded survey landscape used for the 2021 South African population reconstruction, not the roughly 30,000 km2 transfrontier political territory.
records.boundary_source: UNESCO World Heritage dossier 1099bis map and area table; Huffman and Woodborne (2021), Figure 1 and Origins of Mapungubwe Project survey description
records.source_family_independence: The population reconstruction derives from the Origins of Mapungubwe systematic settlement survey and ceramic chronology. SANParks archaeobotanical/archaeozoological synthesis supplies food-regime evidence and UNESCO supplies the protected-property boundary; all are treated as one source family for holdout purposes.
records.notes: This packet supersedes neither the rejected 30,000 km2 polity proxy nor the older 9,000-person heritage summary. It changes the comparison unit: the quantified 2021 South African survey aggregate is tested against its bounded containing EU5 geography. Because the population method is an archaeological reconstruction, the system suffered a severe terminal drought, and food imports cannot be quantified exactly, the only admissible training statement is capacity(mapungubwe EU5 location) >= 10,700.
